full_judgment:
4. The trial court after hearing decreed the suit 

 6. The High Court Division in substance sent back the case on remand to the trial court for fresh trial after setting aside the decree of the said Court and awarding a cost of Tk.3000/- against the defendants. 

 8. We have perused the judgment of the High Court Division. It is full of contradictory statements. It has gone far beyond the prayer made in the revisional application which was only in respect admission of additional evidence by the appellate court. The judgment of the trial court was not the subject matter before the High Court Division. We have noticed that the High Court Division has laboured under the impression that the defendant being a Government machinery deserves absolute lenience in respect of its negligence to bring before the court proper evidence in time. The High Court Division has not given a correct view about the scope of revision under section 115(1) of the Code. Section 115(1) of the Code can be invoked only for correcting error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Section 115 of the Code should not be confused with section 151 thereof. There are other inconsistencies and incoherence in the judgment of the High Court Division which is less said the better. It baffles our comprehension how the High Court Division could have set aside the decree which was not before it to consider. 

 9. In view of the above we are unable to maintain the judgment and order of the High Court Division at least in respect of setting aside the decree of the trial court.
